The Barbarity of Circumcision as a Remedy for Congenital Abnormality is a medical pamphlet by Herbert Snow, surgeon to the Cancer Hospital in London. It was printed at London by Churchill in 1890. The title states the argument plainly: Snow holds the operation, as used for a birth defect of the part, to be a barbarous remedy. His prefatory note opens with a joke against himself.

To say the object of the work is to put down circumcision, Snow writes, would savour of arrogance. It would also recall the too famous alderman who was determined to put down suicide. The practice, as he sees it, inflicts very considerable suffering on helpless infants. It is sanctioned, on extremely questionable grounds, by men of eminent authority. The little book is a surgeon's protest against a routine operation of his day.
